To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the repetition code approach for key generation from noisy PUF responses is not without risk, 2) many of the fuzzy extractors in the literature are not conservative enough, and 3) the parameters of the fuzzy extractor design should be chosen based on the entropy of the PUF and the security requirement.

repetition codes can be used for PUF key generation if the PUF min-entropy is at least 66%, that the entropy loss is underestimated in many fuzzy extractors, and that the leftover entropy of the fuzzy extractor should be at least 128 bits for high security applications.

(i) the entropy loss in PUF based key generation schemes can be very high, (ii) the entropy loss is dependent on the type of PUF, and (iii) the entropy loss can be mitigated with a more accurate estimation of entropy loss.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the question how to extract reliable keys from PUF responses.
the entropy loss that occurs when using PUF-based key generators, and we present a comprehensive analysis of the entropy loss for PUFs with various min-entropy values.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of PUFs for key generation requires careful design and analysis of the entropy extraction process.
the repetition code approach to PUF key generation should be avoided in practice, and that a more careful approach is required to generate reliable keys from memory-based PUFs.
the use of PUFs for key generation should only be considered if the PUF has a min-entropy larger than 66%.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the entropy loss in PUF based key generation schemes must be carefully considered, otherwise a PUF based key could be less secure than the key generated from random bits.
repetition codes are a useful technique for generating keys from memory-based PUFs, but only if the PUFs are sufficiently reliable.
the entropy estimation in PUF-based fuzzy extractors must be carefully considered and that the use of a repetition code in a PUF-based fuzzy extractor is not without risk.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of repetition codes is not without risks, and the entropy loss in PUF based key generation must be carefully estimated.
PUFs are not a silver bullet for secure storage of cryptographic keys.
entropy loss must be considered carefully when using repetition code approaches in key generation schemes.
